A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments with Gemma, GPT-2, and SEDD on four algorithmic tasks, plus summarization experiments on XSUM and CNN/DailyMail.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional sampling comparisons and ablations.

M1.justification: The teacher-forcing and teacherless objectives, hybrid training, and seed-conditioning procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. The additional SEDD variant extends the comparative evaluation without revising the proposed seed-conditioning algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Sibling Discovery, Triangle Discovery, Circle Construction, Line Construction, XSUM, and CNN/DailyMail. The additional sampling experiments retain the existing data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds Diffusion-Uniform alongside Diffusion-Absorb, which corresponds to v2's existing diffusion comparator. Figure 6 removes the GPT-2 pause-prefix comparator; the Gemma pause controls remain in Appendix E.

E3.justification: v2 documents default top-K sampling with K=50 for the small models. v3's Figure 4 instead reports best performance across temperatures {0, 0.5, 1, 2}, with and without top-K. New Appendix F comparisons systematically cross sampling and conditioning settings, substantially changing the evaluation supporting the small-model conclusions.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds systematic analyses separating the effects of training objective, seed-conditioning, top-K truncation, and temperature, including creativity and memorization comparisons in Figures 24–25 and the broader comparisons in Figures 27–28. These substantially extend v2's partial sampling analyses and acknowledged top-K caveat.

E5.justification: The revised Figure 4 removes the error bars displayed in v2. The statement that Gemma results average four runs remains unchanged. This changes uncertainty reporting but does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces the earlier results with tuned-sampling results: diffusion exceeds NTP on all four tasks in v2, but only three in v3, with NTP leading on Sibling Discovery. The Sibling memorization ordering also reverses. Figure 6 changes scores, and Appendix F adds extensive sampling results. These are revised findings under changed settings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The task definitions, creativity and diversity metrics, training objectives, and sample-complexity reasoning remain unchanged, including Appendices A, C, and H. Vocabulary clarification and corrected equation references do not introduce new mathematics or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 removes excessive memorization from the abstract and reduced memorization from the introduction's contribution list. It also frames the creativity advantage as belonging to some multi-token approach rather than uniformly to the alternatives. This materially narrows the claimed general benefits while retaining the task framework and seed-conditioning contribution.

C2.justification: v3 confines the memorization-based explanation primarily to the larger model and interprets teacherless top-K results as evidence of a less peaky distribution. Sections 5.2 and 6.1 expand discussion of post-training, sparse-reward exploration, and uncharacterized model-family and pretraining effects. The underlying latent-planning explanation remains.

D1.justification: New Table 2 documents small-model sequence length, maximum training steps, training sizes, and task-specific objective weights. Several retained appendix plots newly specify greedy decoding. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the underlying training settings; code-access information remains equivalent.

R1.justification: v3 adds Schmidhuber (2009), Muennighoff et al. (2025), Frydenlund (2024), and Hu et al. (2025). The added discussion connects the work to subjective creativity, post-training, and alternative approaches to path-star tasks, without substantially replacing its research positioning.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the diffusion explanation, small-model observations, and reasoning-method discussion, plus terminology, grammar, and cross-reference corrections. Appendix F gains subsections, but the overall organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 6 are redrawn with changed comparator displays, legends, and scales. New Table 2 and four multi-panel sampling figures substantially expand the experimental presentation. Figure 9 corrects sibling-parent labels, while many existing appendix plots are retained and relocated rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The broader sampling controls and appropriately narrowed memorization claims make the small-model evidence more credible, while Table 2 improves reproducibility. The net improvement is tempered by removal of Figure 4's error bars and older top-K descriptions remaining in Section 6.1 and Appendix D without full reconciliation with the revised comparisons. v2 already acknowledged the sampling caveat, so v3 strengthens an existing qualification rather than resolving every reporting issue.
